absent: Host component lock and unlock implementation and any current-state tracking
Numeric values and layouts of donation masks, owner constants, page states and protection bits
Walker callbacks and table node structures for map, unmap, attribute, age and leaf walks
Handle allocation, VM table layout, vcpu to VM linkage and page reference counting internals
Frame validation, allowed-memory checks, host page state accessors and granule sizing
Table memory refill path and minimum-page computation
Firmware workaround probing and secure call effects
Range TLB support detection, maximum range pages and low-level invalidation sequences
Force-entry callback contract and identity-table flag semantics
Program-counter adjustment implementation and register extraction convention

findings.text: Host to guest sharing service provides share, unshare, permission relax, write protect, age test and clear, and mark young operations addressed by guest frame and page count.
Stage2 table service provides map, unmap, single leaf lookup, protection decoding, permission relax, write protect, age handling and mark young plus a VM range flush helper.
VM handle service resolves a handle to a VM object with reference counting, offers a variant that refuses protected VMs, and provides a matching release.
VM context flush is available in two variants for the two hypervisor modes.
Share, relax and mark-young host handlers act on the currently loaded non-protected vcpu, report status to the caller, and refill table memory before sharing.
Unshare, write-protect and age-test host handlers resolve a non-protected VM by handle, run the core operation, release the VM reference and report status.
Two host handlers adjust a vcpu program counter and flush VM context respectively.
Guest component lock acquires a per-VM spin lock and records the VM as current; unlock clears the record before releasing the lock.
Share and unshare hold host and guest components together with host first and release in reverse; relax, write-protect, age and mark-young update the table while holding only the guest component.
A VM table lock serializes handle lookup with reference increment and release with reference decrement.
Guest page-state range checking requires the caller to already hold the per-VM lock.

Donation metadata update refuses the host owner value, requires the range to be memory, requires owner and extra values to fit their fields, then annotates, performs a conditional synchronization and marks pages ownerless.
A range counts as memory only when its start belongs to a known range and its last byte lies in the same range.
Transition size accepts a single page, otherwise exactly one penultimate-level block with both addresses aligned to that block.

Sharing validates requested protections, frame range, transition size and allowed memory before locking; under lock it requires the destination to be unmapped, checks host ownership and share counts, checks table memory, then marks host shared, bumps counts and maps the guest as borrowed.

Unsharing validates transition size, verifies the borrowed mapping and host shared state under both locks, unmaps, decrements per-page counts and restores sole host ownership when a count reaches zero.

Shared mapping verification reads one leaf, requires validity, requires the requested size to match the leaf granule when supplied, requires borrowed guest state and allowed backing memory, requires every host page to be shared with non-zero count, and returns the backing address.
Guest page state reports poison for poisoned invalid entries, absence for other invalid entries, otherwise the state decoded from stage2 protections.
Poison is indicated only by an invalid entry carrying the guest poison marker.
Stage2 mapping rejects identity-table address mismatch, derives entry attributes from the requested protections, walks with table and leaf coverage, then orders with a barrier.

Protection to attribute conversion forbids combining device with non-cacheable, forbids execute with either of those, selects a memory type with a special as-S1 variant, then encodes execute, read, write, shareability, access and software controls.
Execute control encoding needs a hardware capability for split privileged and unprivileged execute and maps the four combinations to distinct two-bit values.
Protection decoding always preserves software bits and adds read, write and execute permissions only for valid entries according to stage2 control fields.
Leaf lookup walks exactly one page with leaf-only coverage and optionally returns the entry and its level.
Unmap walks with leaf and post-table coverage and, when range invalidation plus stage2 write-back caching support hold, does one range flush after the walk.

Relax, write-protect, age and mark-young refuse protected VMs where checked, validate size where applicable, optionally assert shared state in debug builds, then update leaf attributes under the guest lock.
Debug-only shared-state assertion is inactive in normal builds and otherwise revalidates the mapping under both locks, tolerating absence but warning on other mismatches.

Permission relax refuses software bits in the request, converts read, write and execute into set and clear masks, updates a single entry and flushes that address with level or unknown granularity on retry.

Write-protect clears only the stage2 write control over a range while ignoring retry signals; mark-young sets only the access flag for one entry with a barrier on success; age test optionally clears and reports prior youth.
Guest table memory check fails when the vcpu cache holds fewer than the minimum pages required by the VM table.
Host guest metadata packs the VM handle and guest frame number into one value with fit checks.
VM range flush falls back to a full VM flush without range support, otherwise issues chunked range flushes advancing by the flushed length.
Page-state range check walks with a visitor carrying a desired state and a decoding callback; walker coverage is leaf-only for that check.
Page-state check context pairs a desired state with a state decoding callback; table walkers are configured with callback, argument and coverage flags for leaf, table-pre or table-post as needed.
Stage2 map context carries a page-aligned backing address, the owning MMU, a table allocation cache and a forced-entry flag derived from an optional callback.

Host pages move between sole-owned and shared-owned driven by a per-page share count; guest mappings move between unmapped and shared-borrowed; share increments and unshare decrements with sole ownership restored at zero.
Sharing fails busy when a page share count is already at maximum and rejects already multi-shared pages except the tolerated host to non-protected guest case.

Ownership and mapping changes are surrounded by maintenance: donation synchronizes after table maintenance before the owner change, mapping orders with a barrier, and context flush orders before invalidating stage1 entries.
Failures use distinct standard negative results for invalid argument, permission, memory shortage, busy share count, missing mapping and size mismatch.
Execute disable encoding uses four two-bit values for the privileged and unprivileged combinations, and shareability defaults to inner shareable when encoded.
